Operator: Good day, and welcome to the TeleMedia Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you require operator assistance during the call, please press star then zero on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to TeleMedia Corp's Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are John Ramirez, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Network Officer; David Lee, Chief Commercial Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I am excited to share our Q3 results, which reflect our commitment to innovation and customer satisfaction. We achieved strong performance across several key areas.

First, our service revenue growth across wireless, broadband, and enterprise segments exceeded expectations, marking our ninth straight quarter of acceleration. Second, we continue to see strong adoption of our 5G Ultra Fixed Wireless Access and NexStream+ bundles, leading to significant revenue uplift and millions in new subscriber adds. Third, our focus on fiber buildout has driven impressive coverage expansion and customer take rates. Fourth, our operating expense management initiatives delivered substantial savings, enhancing profitability. Fifth, we are strategically optimizing our spectrum assets for higher utilization and future 5G enhancements. And finally, we are exploring new product launches that are supercharging both revenue streams and postpaid growth.

Mike Chen: Thank you, John. Now, let's move on to the financial results. Our revenue for the quarter reached $20.1 billion, an increase of 7.2% compared to the same period last year. Adjusted EBITDA was $10.4 billion, resulting in a margin of 41.8%. We are diligently managing our costs and optimizing our capital allocation. Capital expenditures amounted to $4.5 billion, primarily allocated to 5G infrastructure, fiber deployment, and content acquisition.

Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here, thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call. I'm thrilled to dive into our service revenue performance, which came in at $14.2 billion, up 5.9% year-over-year, or 6.2% on an organic basis excluding foreign exchange headwinds. This underscores the strength of our diversified portfolio across wireless, broadband, and enterprise segments.

Starting with wireless service revenue, which totaled $8.1 billion, up 4.2% YoY. This growth was propelled by subscriber momentum and ARPU expansion in a maturing postpaid market. We added 1.2 million postpaid phone net adds, our strongest quarter since Q1 2022, bringing our industry-leading postpaid phone base to 112 million—a 2.1% YoY increase. Much of this came from our 5G Ultra Wideband network, now covering 285 million people or 89% of the U.S. population, including full mmWave deployment in 25 major metros akin to Verizon's premium footprint.

ARPU grew 2.8% to $52.34, driven by our premium 5G pricing tiers and bundled offerings. For instance, our '5G Max' plans, which bundle unlimited high-speed data with our streaming media services like our co-branded Paramount+ and Peacock partnerships, saw 35% adoption among new adds—lifting blended ARPU by 150 basis points. Churn remained best-in-class at 0.76%, bolstered by our AI-powered customer retention tools, which proactively address service issues via edge analytics.

Regionally, North America drove 85% of the growth, with Mexico contributing a robust 12% YoY wireless surge from our 5G Standalone core rollout in partnership with Nokia, capturing share from legacy 4G competitors. In Europe, our UK joint venture with Vodafone delivered 7% growth amid spectrum refarming to mid-band C-band, though regulatory pricing caps tempered upside. Looking ahead, we're on track for 10 million 5G device upgrades in Q4, fueled by the iPhone 16 cycle and our fixed wireless access expansion to 2 million households, targeting underserved rural pockets where fiber economics don't pencil out.

Turning to broadband service revenue, at $3.4 billion, up a stellar 7.5% YoY—our fastest-growing segment. This reflects aggressive fiber deployments and pricing discipline amid moderating inflation. We passed 18 million locations with our FTTH network, up 25% YoY, achieving gigabit speeds to 12 million homes through our 'Fiber First' initiative, mirroring Comcast's Xfinity blueprint but with 40% lower capex per pass via Open RAN synergies.

Residential broadband added 450,000 net adds, with ARPU climbing 3.1% to $68.22 on 200 Mbps+ tier migrations—now 62% of our base, up from 48% a year ago. Our DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades in legacy cable territories delivered symmetrical 2 Gbps speeds, stemming sub-100 Mbps defections to rivals like T-Mobile's FWA. On the media side, bundling our 100+ linear channels and ad-supported FAST services like our Tubi-like 'TeleStream' app boosted penetration to 45%, adding $4 per sub in ancillary revenue.

Regionally, U.S. Northeast and Sunbelt markets led with 9% growth from greenfield fiber builds in high-growth MSAs like Austin and Phoenix. In Brazil, our Claro JV ramped 1.5 million fiber homes, driving 15% local growth despite FX volatility, while APAC greenfield trials in Indonesia via Starlink backhaul promise 20%+ upside in 2025. Competitively, we're gaining 2 points of share versus cable peers, with churn at 1.1%—the lowest in five years—thanks to our Wi-Fi 7 gateways and AI-driven network slicing for low-latency gaming and remote work.

Finally, enterprise service revenue hit $2.7 billion, growing 6.8% YoY, outpacing the broader IT services market. This segment benefits from our pivot to high-margin, software-defined solutions amid digital transformation tailwinds. Wireless enterprise added 300,000 connections, led by private 5G networks for manufacturing clients—deployments now at 150 sites, similar to our pilots with Ford and Procter & Gamble, leveraging CBRS spectrum for ultra-reliable low-latency comms.

Fixed enterprise grew 5.2%, driven by SD-WAN and SASE adoption, with 25% of our $10 billion mobility backbone now Ethernet-based for cloud on-ramp efficiency. ARPU rose 4.1% to $142, fueled by 400G upgrades and our 'EdgeMedia' platform, which integrates edge computing with content delivery for OTT hyperscalers like AWS and Netflix—capturing 15% more video traffic share. Key wins included a $500 million multi-year deal with a top-5 hyperscaler for private 5G slices and a national retailer's IoT rollout on our LoRaWAN network.

North America accounted for 70% of enterprise growth, with EMEA adding momentum from GDPR-compliant 5G slicing for telco edge services. In Asia, our Singapore hub secured APAC media deals, bundling low-latency CDN with our 5G transport. Strategically, our $2 billion M&A pipeline targets vertical SaaS tuck-ins, like cybersecurity overlays, to lift enterprise EBITDA margins to 45% by 2026.

In summary, service revenue growth of 5.9% YoY reflects balanced execution across segments, with wireless stabilizing, broadband accelerating on fiber, and enterprise compounding via 5G adjacency. Our $18 billion capex plan—65% on wireless modernization, 25% fiber, 10% enterprise—positions us for 6-8% organic growth in 2025, even as spectrum auctions and Open RAN trials de-risk the buildout. We're not just a telco; we're a media-edge-cloud platform, and the market is rewarding that vision.

As we turn to our balance sheet and capital structure, I'm pleased to report continued progress on deleveraging, which positions us exceptionally well for the next phase of growth in our converged telecom and media portfolio. As of September 30th, our consolidated gross debt stood at $128.5 billion, reflecting a modest $1.2 billion increase quarter-over-quarter primarily from revolver draws to fund seasonal working capital in our wireless segment. Net debt, after adjusting for $18.7 billion in cash and short-term investments, came in at $109.8 billion. This represents a net leverage ratio of 2.7x on a last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA basis—our preferred pro forma measure, which excludes one-time items like the $450 million in restructuring charges from our European media integration and adds back synergies from the recent SkyBridge acquisition.

For context, this is a 15 basis point improvement sequentially from 2.85x at Q2 end, and a full turn of deleveraging year-over-year from 3.7x in Q3 2023. On a gross basis, we're at 3.1x, which remains comfortably below our bank covenant threshold of 4.0x and well within investment-grade territory across our $75 billion in senior unsecured notes and $40 billion term loan B facility.

Robust free cash flow generation remains our North Star. LTM Adjusted EBITDA hit a record $40.6 billion, up 8% year-over-year, fueled by mid-teens wireless service revenue growth in North America—where our 5G Standalone core network now covers 95% of our premium postpaid base—and 12% expansion in our streaming and broadband segments. This was partially offset by $14.2 billion in capex, down 5% from last year as we lap peak 5G mid-band spectrum deployment from the 2021 C-band auction. Importantly, our FCFaL reached $12.8 billion LTM, enabling $4.5 billion in debt paydown YTD, including the full redemption of our 4.75% 2024 senior notes.

Debt composition is another strength. About 85% of our debt is fixed-rate, with a blended coupon of 4.1% and an all-in cost of debt of 3.9% after hedges. Our maturity profile is back-end loaded: only 8% matures in the next 12 months, with the bulk—over 60%—not due until 2028 or later. We've proactively managed this through $10 billion in refinancings YTD at sub-4% yields, including a new 10-year senior notes issuance in July at 3.625%, which extended duration by 2.5 years. Floating-rate exposure is limited to 12% on our term loans and revolver, fully hedged via interest rate swaps through 2026 at SOFR + 175 bps.

In North America, which accounts for 65% of EBITDA, net leverage is a pristine 2.3x, supported by our market-leading 5G Ultra Wideband network—now delivering 1 Gbps median speeds—and FTTH expansion to 55 million homes passed via our Xfinity-like hybrid fiber-coax upgrades. This has driven ARPU uplift of 4% and churn below 0.9%, mirroring peers like Comcast and Charter.

In Europe, representing 20% of EBITDA post-SkyBridge, leverage sits at 3.4x due to €5 billion in incremental debt for 700 MHz low-band spectrum wins in the UK's recent auction and initial 5G rollout in Germany and Italy. However, we're realizing €800 million in annual run-rate synergies from content bundling—think our Paramount+ equivalent integrated with Vodafone-like mobile plans—and expect this to delever to 3.0x by year-end through tower monetization. We've already divested €2 billion in non-core macro towers to American Tower equivalents, with more edge data center assets in the pipeline amid rising demand for cloud gaming and AI inference.

Emerging markets, at 15% of EBITDA via our LatAm media and mobile ops, show higher leverage at 4.1x, reflective of Brazil's ongoing 3.5 GHz mid-band buildout and Argentina's inflationary pressures. That said, we've cut net debt there by 20% YTD through local currency bond taps and FX hedges, and our T-Mobile-like prepaid-to-postpaid conversion is yielding 25% EBITDA margins.

This balance sheet firepower—with $15 billion in liquidity, including $8 billion undrawn revolver—gives us dry powder for bolt-on M&A, like potential regional content plays akin to Warner Bros. Discovery's moves, or opportunistic spectrum buys ahead of the FCC's 2024 mmWave auction. We're guiding net leverage to 2.5x-2.7x by FY2024 end, supported by $13-15 billion FCFaL, which funds our $0.85 quarterly dividend yielding 4.2% and $3 billion in share repurchases YTD.

Our disciplined approach to leverage—targeting sub-3.0x long-term—underpins sustainable growth in a capex-intensive industry navigating 5G evolution, fiber overbuilds, and the streaming wars. We're not just maintaining investment-grade metrics; we're building a fortress balance sheet for shareholder returns and tech leadership.

Today, I'd also like to dive deep into our operating expense management initiatives and their direct impact on profitability. In this hyper-competitive telecom and media landscape—amidst ongoing 5G deployments, the streaming wars, and cord-cutting pressures from players like Netflix, Disney+, and our peers at Comcast and Verizon—we've prioritized disciplined OpEx control without compromising service quality or customer growth. Our efforts have delivered $285 million in year-over-year OpEx savings in Q3 alone, driving a 220 basis point expansion in our Adjusted EBITDA margin to 42.3%, and boosting consolidated Adjusted EBITDA by $310 million to $2.1 billion.

First, network operations and modernization, which accounted for 45% of our savings or $128 million. We've accelerated our shift to software-defined networking and network function virtualization, reducing legacy hardware maintenance costs by 28%. For instance, in our U.S. wireless segment—where we're competing head-on with T-Mobile's spectrum advantages—we virtualized 65% of our 4G/5G core, cutting energy consumption by 22% amid rising power costs from data center expansions. This mirrors efficiencies seen at AT&T post-WarnerMedia spin-off. Regionally, in Europe, our Vodafone JV partnership enabled shared Open RAN trials, shaving €45 million in capex-to-Opex leakage, while in APAC, fiber-to-the-x densification in India and Indonesia yielded a 15% OpEx reduction per subscriber, countering Jio's aggressive pricing.

Second, content acquisition and rightsizing, contributing $72 million in savings, or 25% of the total. Media OpEx here has been under intense scrutiny as linear TV viewership declines 12% YoY per Nielsen data. We renegotiated 18 key sports and premium content deals—think NFL Sunday Ticket analogs and UEFA Champions League rights—achieving a 19% average cost reduction through volume bundling and multi-year escalators capped at CPI minus 2%. We also sunsetted 14 underperforming FAST channels, trimming linear distribution costs by $25 million. In streaming, our platform optimized encoding via AV1 codec adoption, dropping bandwidth delivery costs 18% and improving ARPU retention amid Netflix's password crackdown. U.S. savings were strongest at $42 million, driven by Hulu-like bundle synergies, while Latin America's telenovela portfolio rationalization saved $18 million against rising Globo competition.

Third, customer operations and digital transformation, delivering $55 million in savings or 19% of total. Call center and field service costs fell 32% through AI-powered chatbots and predictive maintenance—our GenAI tool, integrated with ServiceNow, resolved 68% of Tier 1 queries autonomously, akin to Verizon's cognitive contact center playbook. This lowered average handle time by 40% and reduced churn-linked support costs. Headcount optimization added $22 million here: we right-sized our U.S. retail footprint by 15% closing 120 stores while upskilling 2,500 employees for 5G enterprise services, maintaining our employee NPS above 75. In EMEA, GDPR-compliant automation saved £12 million, offsetting regulatory fines from the region's DMA enforcement.

Finally, SG&A and procurement efficiencies rounded out the remaining $30 million or 11%. Enterprise-wide zero-based budgeting and supplier consolidation—leveraging our $15 billion annual spend—yielded 14% savings on IT hardware and professional services, with strategic sourcing from Ericsson and Nokia for 5G gear. Inflation hedging via fixed-price contracts mitigated 7% input cost pressures from global supply chain disruptions.

These initiatives not only held OpEx flat QoQ despite 8% revenue growth but expanded our Adjusted EBITDA margin by 220bps. Free cash flow improved $410 million YoY to $1.2 billion, funding $800 million in share repurchases and maintaining our net debt to Adjusted EBITDA at 2.3x—well below Verizon's 2.8x. EPS accreted 18% to $1.42, excluding one-offs.

This positions us for margin expansion to 44-45% by FYE 2025, outpacing Comcast's trajectory. We're doubling down on edge computing for low-latency media delivery and bundling fixed-wireless access with ad-supported streaming to lift broadband ARPU 5-7%. Risks include spectrum auction costs and content blackouts, but our $2.5 billion cash buffer and 40% EBITDA reinvestment flexibility mitigate these. Our OpEx discipline—rooted in tech-led efficiencies and portfolio pruning—has transformed cost headwinds into profitability tailwinds, delivering $285 million in savings and setting the stage for sustained 10-12% annual EBITDA growth.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Mike. I would like to provide an update on our network performance and expansion. We continue to enhance our 5G network, achieving wider coverage and faster speeds. Our network reliability remains high, and we are investing in advanced technologies to further improve performance. We are also focused on optimizing our network for emerging applications like IoT and edge computing.

As we continue to execute on our multi-year fiber-first strategy, I'd like to dive deep into our fiber buildout progress, coverage expansion, and customer adoption metrics. Fiber remains the cornerstone of our network transformation, positioning us to capture high-margin broadband revenue while enabling premium media and entertainment services in an era of 4K/8K streaming, cloud gaming, and AI-driven content delivery.

In Q3, we deployed over 12,500 route miles of fiber—up 28% sequentially from Q2 and 65% year-over-year. This brings our total fiber network footprint to approximately 185,000 route miles, with cumulative capex invested in fiber now exceeding $4.2 billion since our 2021 acceleration plan kicked off. We're leveraging next-gen XGS-PON technology across 85% of new deployments, delivering symmetrical multi-gigabit speeds up to 10 Gbps. Key technical initiatives include our partnership with Nokia for Open RAN-integrated PON overlays, which reduced deployment costs by 15% per mile through automated splicing and drone-assisted surveys. We've also begun piloting 50G PON trials in select Dallas-Fort Worth markets, ahead of widespread rollout in 2025, to future-proof against hyperscale demand from edge computing and VR/AR media applications.

Our homes passed metric grew by 1.2 million in the quarter to a record 18.5 million homes passed nationwide. That's a 22% year-over-year increase, with engineering complete for an additional 2.8 million homes entering Q4 construction queues. Penetration varies by region: Southeast, 35% of total homes passed, adding 450,000 in markets like Atlanta, Charlotte, and Nashville, over-indexing at 42% coverage in greenfield suburbs, capitalizing on lower permitting hurdles and BEAD funding awards totaling $850 million across Georgia and the Carolinas. Midwest, 28%, 380,000 homes added in Chicago exurbs and Indianapolis, taking advantage of rural co-op partnerships mirroring Frontier's model with federal RDOF subsidies. Northeast Urban Core, 20%, 250,000 homes in Boston and Philly via nodalizing legacy copper with micro-trenching to hit 75% coverage in high-RGU density neighborhoods. Western Expansion, 17%, new entry into Phoenix and Denver added 120,000 homes, with plans to scale to 1 million by year-end 2025 via M&A tuck-ins similar to WOW!'s fiber swaps.

This expansion keeps us on track for 25 million homes passed by end-2025, aligning with our $1.2 billion annual fiber capex guidance, which we reaffirmed today despite supply chain stabilization.

Customer adoption tells the real story of monetization. We added 420,000 fiber broadband subscribers in Q3—our best quarter ever—bringing total fiber subs to 6.8 million, up 38% year-over-year. This drove 15% sequential growth in fiber RGUs, including 180,000 video adds bundled with our VeriStream service, which now integrates ad-supported tiers from Peacock and Paramount+ for sticky 70/30 broadband-video attach rates.

Take rates hit 37% overall—expanding 320 basis points quarter-over-quarter—fueled by aggressive promotions like our 'Gig for $70' introductory offer and 2-year price guarantees. In mature markets, homes passed over 3 years, take rates exceed 55%, comparable to AT&T Fiber's footprint, with ARPU holding steady at $128, up 4% YoY on gigabit upgrades and mobile bundling. Churn remains elite at 0.9% monthly, thanks to proactive Net Promoter Score targeting and AI-powered service assurance.

Adoption is accelerating as we lap COVID-era cable cord-cutting; fiber-only households now represent 22% of our broadband base, versus 14% a year ago. Competitively, we're gaining 2.5 share points in fiber-overlaid HFC markets against Comcast's DOCSIS 4.0 push, per Dell'Oro Group data.

Strategically, fiber underpins our 5G fixed wireless access hybrid in rural overshoot areas, covering 1.2 million locations with n78 mmWave backhaul. We're also investing $150 million in media adjacencies, like low-latency CDN nodes for esports leagues and FAST channels, to boost EBITDA margins to 48% in fiber-heavy regions by 2026. Looking forward, Q4 guidance calls for 500,000+ fiber sub adds, with homes passed hitting 20 million. Risks remain around labor inflation and municipal right-of-way delays, but our $2.5 billion liquidity and recent $1 billion green bond issuance provide ample dry powder.

I'd also like to spend some time on one of our most valuable strategic assets: our spectrum portfolio. Spectrum remains the lifeblood of our telecommunications and media ecosystem, powering everything from our nationwide 5G Standalone network to our high-margin fixed wireless access services and low-latency content delivery for streaming partners like Netflix and Disney+. In an era of exploding data demand—driven by 4K/8K video streaming, cloud gaming, AR/VR applications, and the proliferation of IoT devices—our spectrum strategy is central to sustaining our competitive moat against peers like Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile.

As of quarter-end, we hold approximately 285 MHz of average spectrum depth per POP across the U.S., with a premium focus on mid-band assets. This includes 120 MHz in the C-band (3.7-4.2 GHz), acquired at a blended cost of $0.45 per MHz-POP in the 2021 FCC Auction 107; 80 MHz in the 2.5 GHz band from our legacy Clearwire integration; and 85 MHz across sub-1 GHz low-band for coverage reliability. We're also leaders in mmWave with over 2,200 licenses totaling 1.2 GHz in key urban markets, positioning us ahead of the curve for ultra-high-capacity enterprise solutions.

Utilization rates are strong and trending upward, reflecting disciplined network densification and software-defined optimization. Overall, our spectrum utilization stands at 76% on an average basis across our 5G footprint, up from 68% a year ago. Low-band (600 MHz and 850 MHz): 82% utilization, primarily for wide-area coverage, handling baseline IoT traffic, which grew 45% YoY to 15% of total payload, and supports our rural FWA deployments, now serving 1.2 million households with median speeds of 150 Mbps down/50 Mbps up.

Mid-band (C-band and 2.5 GHz): 74% utilization, delivering the sweet spot for capacity and propagation. Here, 5G NR traffic accounts for 62% of total mobile data, with peak throughputs exceeding 1.2 Gbps in deployed SA mode. Video streaming—optimized via our Media Edge Network—comprises 55% of mid-band usage, a testament to partnerships with hyperscalers like AWS and content giants.

High-band (mmWave): 68% utilization in 45 top DMAs, where we're achieving gigabit symmetrical speeds for enterprise private 5G networks. Adoption here is accelerating, with private network revenue up 120% YoY to $450 million annualized, fueled by manufacturing verticals like automotive pilots with Ford for V2X communications.

Geographically, utilization varies by density. In the Northeast Corridor (NYC, Boston, Philly), we're at 89% overall, constrained by population density exceeding 5,000 people per sq. mi. and data consumption 2.5x the national average. In the Midwest (Chicago exurbs and Great Plains), 62%, offering headroom for aggressive FWA expansion targeting 3 million additional subs by 2026. In the Sun Belt (Florida, Texas), 81%, supporting post-disaster recovery services that generated $120 million in incremental revenue last year.

Mobile data traffic surged 28% YoY to 12 EB quarterly, outpacing our 22% capacity expansion. ARPU uplift from 5G premium plans hit +$4.50, now 18% of our postpaid base. Our spectral efficiency has improved 15% via Massive MIMO 32T32R upgrades and AI-driven dynamic spectrum sharing, squeezing 25% more throughput from existing holdings versus 2023 baselines.

Our $2.8 billion Capex plan for FY24 allocates 40%—$1.1 billion—to spectrum-related initiatives: refarming and carrier aggregation—we've refarmed 100% of our legacy 3G/2G spectrum (20 MHz nationwide) to 5G NR by Q2-end, unlocking 12% immediate capacity gains. Dynamic Spectrum Sharing between 4G LTE and 5G is live in 85% of our footprint, with plans for full 5G SA migration by Q4 2025, reducing latency to sub-10ms for media applications like live sports streaming.

Network slicing for media and enterprise: leveraging 3GPP Release 16, end-to-end slicing on C-band—one slice for URLLC in private networks (50ms latency for industrial automation with Siemens partners), another for eMBB video at 4K60fps with zero buffering. This has boosted media partner satisfaction scores to 95% NPS.

CBRS and Open RAN integration: in the 3.5 GHz CBRS band, we've deployed 15,000 small cells via SAS automation, achieving 92% uptime. Pairing this with Open RAN from Nokia and Samsung cuts OpEx by 18% while enabling rapid spectrum arbitrage.

Looking ahead, our spectrum roadmap targets 320 MHz average depth per POP by 2027, blending organic optimization with opportunistic inorganic growth. Short-term (2024-2025): $800 million bid capacity for FCC Auction 110 (3.45-3.55 GHz) and potential Lower 3 GHz opportunities, prioritizing top 100 DMAs for mid-band fill-up. We'll allocate 40 MHz of refarmed assets to FWA nationwide, aiming to convert 20% of our 15 million cable households to hybrid bundles, driving $1.2 billion in incremental EBITDA.

Medium-term (2026+): heavy emphasis on mmWave expansion via secondary markets and partnerships—e.g., JV talks with Charter Spectrum for shared urban deployments—and 6G pathfinding in sub-THz bands. Internationally, eyeing Mexico's IFT auctions for cross-border C-band harmony, supporting our growing enterprise footprint.

This positions us at the intersection of telecom and media. Unlike pure-play wireless carriers, our 28 million video subs provide a captive audience for spectrum-intensive services like bundled 5G home internet (now 35% take rate) and ad-supported streaming tiers. We're modeling 10-12% CAGR in spectrum-driven revenue through 2028, with ROIC exceeding 15% on new allocations. Risks include regulatory delays and competitive bidding, but our $18 billion liquidity and proven auction track record mitigate that. Our spectrum assets are highly utilized, efficiently managed, and primed for value-unlocking reallocations. This underpins our raised FY24 guidance: adjusted EBITDA of $14.5-14.8 billion, up 8% at midpoint.

David Lee: Thank you, Lisa. I'm excited to share our commercial achievements. We saw strong growth in subscriber additions, driven by our innovative product offerings and targeted marketing campaigns. Customer satisfaction remains a top priority, and we are continuously working to improve the customer experience across all touchpoints. We are also focused on expanding our partnerships to offer bundled services and enhance customer value.

Before I dive into the segment results, I'd like to highlight the standout performance from our new product and service launches, which have been a key driver of both revenue acceleration and subscriber momentum this quarter. We've been aggressively executing our 'Connect & Stream' strategy, leveraging our nationwide 5G SA network and media assets to capture share in the converged telecom-media market.

On revenue contribution: Our new launches generated $1.2 billion in incremental revenue during Q3, representing a 28% quarter-over-quarter increase from Q2's $938 million and a robust 52% year-over-year growth. This outpaced our overall service revenue growth of 7% YoY, underscoring the high-margin profile of these initiatives.

5G Ultra FWA: Our flagship broadband alternative to fiber, now available in 45 major MSAs with mid-band C-band spectrum delivering up to 1 Gbps symmetric speeds. This drove $675 million in new revenue—up 35% QoQ—fueled by an ARPU of $85/month, 15% higher than our traditional DSL base. Penetration in eligible markets hit 22%, ahead of our 20% target, as we targeted cord-cutters switching from cable incumbents like Comcast Xfinity.

NexStream+ Bundle: Our ad-supported streaming service, bundling live sports, premium OTT content via partnerships with Peacock and Paramount+, and our linear TV channels. This added $325 million in revenue, with 42% from new advertising dollars—our AVOD inventory sold out at a $25 CPM, 18% above industry benchmarks per IAB data. Subscription revenue here grew 31% QoQ to $190 million.

Edge Media Platform: An AI-driven edge computing service for low-latency content delivery, integrated with our MEC nodes. Early enterprise wins with gaming studios and live event broadcasters contributed $200 million, with 65% from recurring SaaS contracts at $0.02 per GB delivered—a new high-margin stream rivaling hyperscalers like AWS Outposts.

Overall, these launches boosted our total wireless service revenue by 9% YoY to $14.5 billion and fixed broadband by 12% to $4.8 billion, with blended ARPU expanding 2.7% to $58.50. EBITDA margins on these new streams averaged 52%, well above our company-wide 45%, thanks to opex efficiencies from network slicing and AI-optimized traffic routing.

Turning to subscriber growth, we added a net 2.8 million postpaid subscribers across these launches—smashing our guidance of 2.0 million and marking our best Q3 in five years. This brought our total postpaid base to 118 million, with churn at a record low of 0.72%, down 15 bps YoY, as bundling reduced multi-product churn by 22%.

FWA subscribers: 1.6 million net adds (up 40% QoQ), concentrated in the U.S. Sunbelt regions like Texas and Florida, where broadband penetration lags at 85% vs. the national 92% per FCC stats. We're now at 4.2 million FWA subs, with 75% coming from competitive wins against Charter and AT&T Fiber—our Wi-Fi 6E gateways have been a game-changer for gigabit households.

NexStream+: 850,000 net adds, with 65% from broadband bundling. In Europe, via our Vodafone joint venture, we gained 220,000 in the UK and Germany, capitalizing on the EU's Digital Markets Act pushing open access to premium content. APAC pilots in India added 45,000, partnering with Jio for Hindi-localized sports streaming.

Edge Media: 350,000 enterprise 'virtual subs' (measured as active API sessions), primarily in media workflows for latency-sensitive apps like AR/VR concerts.

Regionally, U.S. drove 75% of adds (2.1 million), with Latin America contributing 15% (420,000) through our millennial-targeted mobile bundles in Brazil and Mexico. Europe lagged at 8% due to regulatory headwinds on spectrum auctions, but we're on track for acceleration in Q4 with 6GHz unlicensed rollout.

These launches position us squarely against disruptors like T-Mobile's FWA push and Starlink's satellite broadband, while our media integration differentiates us from pure-plays like Verizon. We've seen ARPU uplift of $4.20 from cross-sell synergies, with 68% of FWA customers adopting NexStream+ within 90 days. Looking ahead, we expect these to contribute $5.5-6.0 billion in FY25 revenue, with subscriber adds of 10-11 million, supported by CapEx discipline—our 5G SA coverage now at 85% of POPs, enabling virtualized network functions to scale without proportional opex.

This momentum validates our pivot to converged services amid cord-cutting (U.S. pay-TV subs down 5% YoY per Nielsen) and 5G monetization.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your subscriber acquisition costs and your strategy for reducing churn, specifically with regards to your new FWA offerings?

David Lee: Thanks, Emily. On subscriber acquisition costs, we're seeing SAC for FWA come in at around $450, down 12% YoY due to digital-first marketing and bundling efficiencies with NexStream+, which has driven 68% attach rates. For churn reduction, our AI retention tools and Wi-Fi 6E gateways have kept FWA churn at 1.1%, below industry averages, by proactively slicing networks for gaming and streaming. We're targeting further SAC compression through partner referrals with content providers like Peacock, aiming for sub-$400 by year-end.
